summary_en: ¥10/share FY3/27 (prior guidance ¥5/share). Payout ratio target raised to 50%+ from 30%+. Calculation metric shifted from reported net income to adjusted net income (add-back: goodwill amortization ~¥1.3B p.a., tax adjustments). Policy change reflects asset-light model cash generation and capital efficiency priorities.
title_en: Notice regarding revision of shareholder return policy and upward revision of FY3/27 dividend forecast (dividend increase)
translation_en_brief:
Polaris Holdings announced on 24 June 2026 a revision to its shareholder return policy and upward revision of FY3/27 dividend guidance. The board approved raising the FY3/27 dividend forecast from ¥5/share to ¥10/share, doubling the prior guidance.

The policy revision reframes the payout-ratio calculation metric. Previously, Polaris used reported net income under Japanese GAAP as the denominator. Going forward, it will shift to "adjusted net income," defined as reported net income plus goodwill amortization (~¥1.3 billion annually from the Minacia business combination) plus deferred tax adjustments. This adjustment reflects the company's asset-light hotel operating model, which generates substantial cash flow but carries non-cash accounting charges that depress reported profit.

Simultaneously, Polaris raised its consolidated payout-ratio target to 50%+ from the prior 30%+. Management states this increase reflects the company's underlying earnings and cash generation capacity, and balances financial soundness, growth investment, and shareholder distributions. The company remains open to opportunistic hotel acquisitions or M&A if market conditions offer significant discounts and strong long-term return potential.
